## Before the bench {.center}

### What you are about to measure

You have a generator that swings above and below zero, and a board that
accepts $0$–$3.3$ V.

By the end of the session you will know:

- how to design the stage that reconciles the two, and what its own
  uncertainty costs you;
- exactly which apparent frequency a given generator frequency folds to, and
  why that is predictable but not detectable after the fact;
- what an anti-alias filter buys you, in decibels, and what it costs the
  passband to buy it;
- why a digital filter, applied after sampling, can clean up an oversampled
  signal but can never undo an alias.

### The rule of the session

::: {.callout-important}
## Prevention, not correction

Every other error in this course can be measured, bounded and corrected after
the fact. Aliasing cannot. The moment a signal above $f_s/2$ is sampled, the
information that would distinguish it from a lower-frequency signal is gone —
not hidden, not recoverable with a cleverer filter, gone. The only lever is
upstream of the ADC.
:::

## At the bench {.center}

### What you will build

A conditioning stage, sized from @eq-s3-gain-offset for your generator's
amplitude and the ADC's input range, and (optionally) a filter stage ahead of
it.

::: {.smaller}
| Run(s) | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Aliasing sweep, 16 frequencies at one fixed $f_s$ | The folding triangle: predicted vs. observed $f_a$ |
| Filtered / unfiltered pair, one frequency above $f_s/2$ | What a real filter's attenuation actually buys |
| Oversampled run, signal + interferer | Input to the digital-filtering section |
:::

### Then

Open [the handbook](handbook.qmd) for the full procedure, and one of the two
analysis templates — [Python](analysis-py.qmd) or [R](analysis-r.qmd).

They have the same sections and produce the same numbers. Both ship with
reference data, so you can read the whole analysis before you wire anything.

## What you should come away with {.center}

### Three sentences you should be able to defend

1. "Our conditioning stage maps $\pm V_g$ onto $[V_\mathrm{lo}, V_\mathrm{hi}]$
   with gain $G = \dots$ and offset $V_\mathrm{off} = \dots$, verified at DC
   to within $\dots$ of the design targets."
2. "At $f_s = \dots$ Hz, a generator frequency of $\dots$ Hz folds to
   $\dots$ Hz, and our measurement agreed with that prediction to within
   $\dots$ Hz."
3. "Our filter attenuated the folded component by $\dots$ dB, against a
   design target of $\dots$ dB at $\dots$ Hz, and the cost in the passband
   was $\dots$ dB of droop at $\dots$ Hz."

If you can say those three with your own numbers in them, the session worked.
